sentences.text: The petitioner is a proprietary concern, which is conducting an industrial unit manufacturing Vermicelli and allied food products at Mini Industrial Estate, Kanniyampuram, Ottapalam.

The dispute involved in this writ petition pertains to the notice of termination issued by the 2nd respondent and the notice of eviction issued, directing the petitioner to vacate the building where the proprietary concern is housed.
The Mini Industrial Estate, where the petitioner is running its business belongs to the Kerala State Small Industries Development Corporation.

entities.text: Kerala State Small Industries Development Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Earlier, one N.Suryanarayanan was allotted with the building, which is the subject matter of the dispute.

Thereafter, the said Suryanarayanan entered into a partnership deed with one A.S.
Sidharthan, the father of the 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 proprietor of the petitioner firm.
Ext . P1
is the deed of partnership entered into between the parties.
Ext . P2

is the Articles of Agreement entered into between the Kerala State Small Industries Development & Employment Corporation Ltd. (SIDCO) with the said N.Suryanarayanan as well as Sri.A.S. Sidharthan, for the purpose of allotment of the said building for running M/s.Kamadhenu Food Products.

entities.text: Kerala State Small Industries Development & Employment Corporation Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On the basis of the same, the said partnership firm was running its business in the building and later, as per Ext.P3 the partnership was reconstituted by which, the said Suryanarayanan exited from the partnership and it was being continued as a proprietary concern of Sri.A.S. Sidharthan.
The said Sidharthan passed away on 14.10.2005 and thereafter, the son of the said Sidharthan is continuing the said establishment in the said building.

Ext.P8 termination notice was issued by the 1st respondent on 14.11.2014 stating that, the petitioner is in 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 unauthorized occupation of the building, as the allotment of the building stands in the name of Sri.N. Suryanarayanan, who is no more.
Even though the petitioner submitted Ext.P9 in response to Ext.P8, Ext.P10 order was issued by the 1 st respondent reiterating the stand taken in Ext.P8.
Based on Ext.P10, Ext.P11 notice was also issued intimating that, the petitioner will be evicted on 25.09.2015.
It was in these circumstances this writ petition is submitted alleging Exts.P8, P10 and P11.

3. I have heard Sri.Ravi K.(Pariyarath), learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri.R.T. Pradeep,
learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.
4. The main contention raised by the learned Counsel for the petitioner is that, Exts.P8, P10 and P11 were issued without properly considering the documents available on record.

It is pointed out that,
Ext.P8 was issued by the 1 st 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 respondent stating that,
the allotment was made to Sri.N. Suryanarayanan and he is no more.

On the other hand, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, by placing reliance upon Ext.P2, which is the articles of agreement,
entered into between the SIDCO on one side and the said Suryanarayanan and said Sidharthan on the other side, would contend that the said documents clearly indicate that, a contractual relationship was created by the SIDCO, with respect to the allotment of the said property with the said Sidharthan as well, who is the father of the proprietor of the petitioner firm herein.
On perusal Ext.P2 it can be seen that, name of A.S. Sidharthan is also specifically referred to therein.
It is also discernible therefrom that, the name of the unit is mentioned as "Kamadhenu Food Products" and it is referred to as a partnership firm.

The petitioner is even now functioning in the very same name even though the constitution of the same 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 was changed to that of a proprietary concern, consequent to the retirement of one of the earlier partners.

Apart M/S. Kamadhenu Food Products vs The Head (O[/Mie/Ie) Division on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124839927/
2 from the above, in Ext.P9 reply submitted by the petitioner to Ext.P8, details are furnished, relating to the transactions that took place after the retirement of Sri.N.Suryanarayanan as the partner of the said firm and the continued ownership of Sri.A.S. Sidharthan over the property.

entities.text: Kamadhenu Food Products vs The Head (O[/Mie/Ie) Division
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the death of said Sidharthan, the petitioner, who is the son of the said person is running the said establishment and the said fact is also not apparently disputed.
Even though all these details are specifically furnished, the same is not seen considered in any of the orders passed by the 1st respondent.

The fact that, the name of Sri.A.S. Sidharthan, the predecessor in interest of the petitioner, is mentioned in Ext.P2 agreement in which the 1st respondent is a party, is something very crucial and the said fact is also not seen referred to in Ext.P8 termination 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 notice.

Therefore, I find force in the submission made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner to the effect that, the said order was passed without any application of mind and without properly examining the documents maintained by the respondents.
In such circumstances, an interference is required.
Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of quashing Exts.P8, P10 and P11 with a direction to the respondents to reconsider the matter, after giving the petitioner an opportunity for being heard.
Further orders shall be passed after specifically adverting to the contentions raised by the petitioner in Ext.P9.
Such orders shall be passed as expeditiously as possible.
